source_locator: R2225: ch. VII, Aola Bay, and ch. VIII, Koli Point
current_activity: landing unopposed at Aola Bay with the Aola Force
notes: Miller, ch. VII: the Aola Force, including two companies of the 2nd Raider Battalion, landed unopposed at Aola Bay on 4 November 1942 and established a 600-yard beachhead east of the Aola River, after which command passed to Vandegrift. Chapter VIII and the caption date Carlson’s Raiders at Aola on the morning of 4 November and their later overland march toward Koli Point. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment (Zimmerman, ch. VIII, describes the landing and patrol but was not used as a second-family read for the calendar date here).

current_activity: entering the Lunga perimeter after a 30-day march from Aola Bay
notes: Miller, ch. VIII: after landing at Aola Bay on 4 November, Carlson’s 2nd Raider Battalion marched west, harrying Japanese moving inland from Koli Point, covered 150 miles, fought 12 actions, and killed over 400 Japanese at a cost of 17 raiders killed, before entering the Lunga perimeter on 4 December. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.
